note: Phase 2 closes what it can prove and defers the rest explicitly. Every Phase 2 function row in inventory.json appears exactly once below, and validate_inventory.py enforces that, recomputes the counts, checks every gate against the real target registry, and rejects a closure that claims a falsification it does not carry. There is one proof kind per gate and both require a mutation: the proof kinds that rested on a free-text observation were deleted, because a run can name a real step and still never enter the row, and every error review found was one of those rows. The 48 rows they carried were re-measured by a mutation probe; 5 of them could not produce a detection and were demoted here rather than kept. Where the guarantee ends: recomputed counts and a required non-zero mutation delta make the strongest claim the costly one, but they do not make a false one impossible. The probe transcripts are not committed artifacts, so a fabricated mutation string with a plausible delta beside it would pass this validator. What is checked is that a claim of the shape exists and is internally consistent; what is not checked is that the run behind it happened. Two further limits are in the numbers themselves. Most of these deltas come from an entry probe -- a print at the top of the row -- so what they establish is that the gate enters the row, which is what the deleted kind asserted without checking; they do not establish that the gate would notice the row computing the wrong answer. And a static_proof_falsified row has no oracle side at all: it is checked against expectations read out of the disassembly, so it is only as good as that reading. One row is closed by a later phase: phys_fn_001690 was deferred homeless_shared_code with driving_phases [3, 4] because no Phase 2 entry point reaches it, and Phase 3's capsule/capsule entries are the reachability it lacked. It stays a Phase 2 row -- ownership is a census fact and the stray rule keeps one row owned by exactly one phase -- and what moved is the proof, so it is recorded here with discharged_by_phase rather than on Phase 3's ledger. Three more rows were closed that way by the canonical line -- phys_fn_002410, phys_fn_002404 and phys_fn_002406, discharged_by_phase 5 on Phase 5's NxPhysicsObjectLayoutTests -- and all three were RE-DEFERRED at the port of the Phase 4 close: a discharge counts only once the discharging phase has passed, Phase 5 has not, and so no passing gate runs their proofs. They are blocked_on_later_phase with their mutations, counts, source commits and dirty-control readings in their notes, for a Phase 5 close to discharge. phys_fn_001690, discharged by Phase 3, which has passed, is the only row a later phase has closed here. P4 Task 1c removed 19 rows from this ledger because the census no longer gives them to Phase 2: 14 qhull rows, phys_fn_004886 of IcePrunable.cpp, and phys_fn_004836/004840/004846/004847, which the source correspondence map identifies as OPCODE Ice/IceContainer.cpp members. The last four were closed here on static proofs; those proofs measured real behaviour and are reproduced in gates/phase2.json as the third_party_container_rows_moved escalation, but the ledger entry that authorised their inventory state left with the row, so the four are back at 'reconstructed' and Phase 4 has to close them again. Every remaining number here is recomputed from the entries below.

proof_kinds.static_proof_falsified: a mutation was aimed at this row and the static-proof gate failed the named check; there is no oracle side, so this is weaker than any differential
proof_kinds.oracle_differential_falsified: a mutation was aimed at this row's reconstruction in a throwaway tree, rebuilt, and run through an oracle differential -- a target that loads the pinned DLL in its own process, checks its hash, and calls the recorded internal address directly; the recorded mismatches count is what that target reported against the shipped bytes. Phase 2 has no such target of its own, so every closure of this kind carries discharged_by_phase naming the later phase whose gate produced it, and that phase must be one the original deferral listed in driving_phases and must stand at `pass` in program.json: a discharge counts only once the discharging phase has passed

RE-DEFERRED at the port of the Phase 4 close (branch p4-close-port), for the reason phys_fn_002344 was re-deferred on the Phase 3 ledger: a closure counts only once the phase whose gate it rests on has passed. Canonical commit e7094e9 closed this row on Phase 5's NxPhysicsObjectLayoutTests with `discharged_by_phase: 5` and `driving_phases: [3, 5, 6, 7]`. NxPhysicsObjectLayoutTests is registered to phase 5 only and Phase 5 is `pending` in program.json, so it runs neither when Phase 2 is gated nor under `-Phase completed`, and the validator now rejects a discharge by a phase that has not passed. No passing gate executes this row's proof. The deferral the closure came from was homeless_shared_code with driving_phases [3, 5, 6, 7]; that list is kept, and Phase 3 passed without discharging the row. It is blocked on the Actor: it is the constructor of the actor's +0x08 member subobject, and the only fixture that drives it is Phase 5's actorctor, through phys_fn_000044, the actor construction tail that calls it at 0x00002496. MUTATION, from e7094e9: the +0x08 member subobject constructor stops zeroing its two fields after the third-table vptr store. Detected on actorctor: the construction-tail drive reads 0xcdcdcdcd where the image leaves zeros. Control run of the unmutated tree reads mismatches=1 (the designed vtables RED), this run mismatches=2. DETECTED, from e7094e9: mismatches=2. RE-MEASURED at this re-deferral in a `git archive` copy of d9a459b, control / mutant / control: `layout candidate mismatches=1`, then `2`, then `1`, with `layout oracle digest=16dceb3c` in all three; the mutant moves actorctor alone, `ok=1 ct=1/1/1/1/1 ... digest=19f4915a` to `ok=0 ct=1/1/1/0/1 ... digest=829d440b`. THE CONTROL IS NOT CLEAN: its one mismatch is `candidate CANDIDATE-MISSING family=vtables`, the target's designed RED, so a target-level count is a count over a baseline of 1 and the part of it this row owns is the family reading. A Phase 5 discharge must re-establish a control in which the count it spends starts at zero, or spend the family-level reading, rather than inherit a target-level baseline that was already off
